fixes.bug: 1a. Links in emails take their address from whoever made the latest request when APP_URL is not set (HIGH)
fixes.how: src/server/util.ts setOrigin(): with APP_URL set it does nothing; without it, a request origin is kept only when its hostname is localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (http/https). Any other host is ignored and one loud console.error says to set APP_URL; baseUrl() then stays at http://localhost:3000 (or the localhost address seen earlier). Host / X-Forwarded-Host can no longer reach an email or a stored link. ctx.origin is kept for same-browser answers; I checked every baseUrl() and c.origin use in src/server (c.origin is used by no handler, no page builds URLs from headers). README config table and .env.example now say APP_URL is required on a real deployment. Seen live in a dev server: verify link pointed at http://localhost:3411, a forged X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example changed nothing and logged the warning once.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'links in emails never take their address from a request header' (password reset with forged X-Forwarded-Host, timer reminder after forged Host, warning printed exactly once, localhost still believed and not overwritten, APP_URL wins). Fails when the localhost-only condition is removed.

The address is the entry that many places from the right of X-Forwarded-For; a shorter list uses its first entry (still proxy-written); 0 ignores the header and gives 'unknown'. X-Real-IP is no longer read at all. Documented in README and .env.example.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'the address of a caller is the one our proxy saw, not one the caller typed' (unit cases for 0/1/2 hops, plus 11 password-reset requests with a new invented first entry each time: the 11th is 429). Fails when the first entry is used.

fixes.bug: 2a. Lower-case bearer is rejected as if no key was sent; every key failure answered 'Please sign in.'
fixes.how: src/server/auth.ts authenticate(req, required): scheme matched in any case. On routes that need sign-in a key problem is thrown with its own message: 401 header could not be read (how to send it), 401 key unknown or revoked, 401 key stopped because its creator left the account (with the date), 403 account being closed. 'Please sign in.' remains only when nothing was sent. A non-key Authorization header plus a valid session cookie still uses the session; public routes ignore the header. openapi.ts security scheme now describes these answers, so the 'errors say what to do' claim holds for keys.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'an API key that cannot be used says what is wrong, and "bearer" may be in any case'. Fails without the i flag and when the key-specific refusals are removed.

fixes.bug: 2b. An API key carries its creator's whole role, with no narrower permission
fixes.how: New column api_keys.scope (default 'send', so old rows are 'send'). POST /api-keys takes scope; 'admin' must be named and only an admin may ask (403 otherwise, 400 for anything else). router.ts enforces in one place: a 'send' key is refused on every admin-level route (403 that names the scope and what to do), except GET /webhooks, where the handler returns secret: null for it. PERSON_ONLY list, matched on the route pattern, blocks every key of either scope from: POST/DELETE /api-keys, POST /account/transfer-owner, DELETE /account/members/:id, POST /me/delete, every non-GET /billing/* route, and /operator/*. Scope is returned by POST and GET /api-keys and shown as a badge in the key list. The settings screen replaces the name prompt with a dialog: name, Send or Admin, and a warning box when Admin is chosen.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'a key gets the "send" scope unless "admin" is asked for, and some things no key can do' (send key does everyday work, is refused on invites, account, webhooks; reads webhooks without secrets; admin key works on settings but gets 403 on keys, transfer, remove member, close, cancel, refund, redeem, checkout, top-up; old row is 'send'). Fails when either router check or the secret masking is removed.
fixes.left_open: By design of the brief an 'admin' key can still invite a person as admin and change member roles; the dialog warning says so. fixes.bug: 2c. Removing a team member silently deletes their API keys and breaks whatever used them
fixes.how: Keys are no longer deleted on removal: new column api_keys.stopped_at marks them, they stay on the admins' list as stopped and never revive if the person rejoins. GET /api-keys gives admins every key in the account (name, prefix, scope, owner name and email, last used, stopped_at, mine), members only their own; the secret is never stored so never returned. DELETE /account/members/:id answers { ok, keys_stopped: [...] } and, when there are any, emails every other admin and the removed person naming the keys. Admins can revoke or clear any key in the account. Team tab: the Remove dialog lists the keys that stop, with last use, and the toast repeats them. Checked in a browser (dialog, toast, stopped rows, both emails in the outbox).

fixes.bug: 2d. API keys keep working, and keep sending, after the account was closed
fixes.how: authenticate() refuses a key with 403 while accounts.closing_at or the key owner's users.closing_at is set. The message says the account (or the creator's login) is being closed, the date before which nothing is deleted, and that signing in restores it. Signing in clears closing_at (existing behaviour), and the key works again.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'API keys are switched off while an account is being closed, and work again when it is restored' (read and send refused, no email goes out, restored after login, team member closing their own login). Fails when the closing check is removed.

fixes.bug: 3a. Failed webhook deliveries become impossible to send again because other customers' traffic erases them
fixes.how: src/server/webhooks.ts deliver(): the row is inserted before the first try (new column webhook_deliveries.done = 0, body stored) and updated after each try, so there is one row per delivery and an in-flight event survives a restart; a row still not done after 2 minutes is shown as failed with 'The server restarted before this delivery finished. Send it again.' and can be resent. Bodies are pruned per webhook (latest 200 of EACH webhook, new index on (webhook_id, id)). GET /webhooks takes ?webhook= and ?before=, returns 30 rows a page with state (pending / delivered / failed), can_redeliver and next_before. Redeliver answers 409 while still being tried and a clear 400 for rows older than the 200. The 'Nothing is lost' email is reworded to what is kept. Settings screen: filter per webhook, 'Show older deliveries', 'Trying now' rows; developers page and openapi updated.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'a webhook delivery is in the log from before the first try, and can be sent again after a restart', 'what can be sent again is counted per webhook, and the log has pages', and the email wording in 'a redirect is not followed, and the email about a failing webhook promises only what is kept'. Each fails with the old prune statement, without the early row, without paging, or with the old email text.
fixes.left_open: An interrupted delivery is not retried by itself after a restart; a person sends it again from the log. Events older than the latest 200 of a webhook cannot be resent (email, screen and docs now say so). Log rows themselves are never deleted, and rows of a deleted webhook stay in the table unseen (both as before).

fixes.bug: 3b. Webhook address check can be bypassed by a hostname that changes its answer
fixes.how: resolvePublic() looks the name up once (10 second limit), refuses if any answer is private, and returns the checked addresses; post() uses node:http/https request with agent: false and a lookup function that returns only those addresses, so Host header and TLS server name stay the host name. Redirects are not followed, one 10 second deadline covers the whole exchange, the reply is discarded and cut off after 64 KB. One refusal message for 'does not resolve' and 'not public'. I also added the per-account cap the audit asked for (20 webhooks). With ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS=1 the name is still resolved once and pinned, and only http/https are accepted.
fixes.test: tests/platform.test.ts: 'a webhook is sent to the address that was checked, with one answer for every address that is refused' (five refused addresses give one identical message; a name that flips to 127.0.0.1 is refused at delivery time; a name that exists only in the stubbed lookup is delivered with one lookup and the right Host header; an endless reply is cut off; the 21st webhook is refused) and the redirect test. Fails without the pinned lookup, with two messages, without the size cut-off, without the cap.
fixes.left_open: TLS server name and certificate check against the host name, and the 10 second timeout, were verified by hand with a self-signed certificate and a hanging server (correct name 200, wrong name rejected by the certificate check, 'No answer within 10 seconds.' after 3 tries), not in the suite: the timeout case takes 36 seconds and the TLS case needs a certificate. I return every checked address rather than a single one so dual-stack hosts keep working; all of them passed the check. isPrivate() itself is unchanged and still misses some special ranges (for example 198.18.0.0/15, NAT64).

New settings and behaviour to know before deploying:
- APP_URL is now required on a real host. Without it every email link points at http://localhost:3000 and one warning is logged.
- TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS (default 1) must match the real number of proxies. Too low (for example a CDN plus the platform router with the default 1) makes every caller look like the inner proxy, so all visitors share one rate-limit bucket (login is 30 per 15 minutes). Too high lets a caller choose their address. Check what X-Forwarded-For looks like in production before launch. X-Real-IP is no longer read.
- Existing API keys become scope "send": they lose admin-level routes. No key can call POST/DELETE /api-keys, transfer-owner, DELETE /account/members/:id, POST /me/delete, any non-GET /billing/* route, or /operator/* (this also covers the new GET /operator/billing/lookup).
- Response shapes changed: GET /api-keys (scope, owner_name, owner_email, stopped_at, mine; admins get all keys), POST /api-keys returns scope, DELETE /account/members/:id returns keys_stopped, GET /webhooks deliveries now have state and a boolean can_redeliver plus next_before, and secret is null for a "send" key. Admins can now revoke any key in the account.
- An Authorization header that is not one of our keys, with no session cookie, now gets a 401 about the header rather than 'Please sign in.' (a signed-in browser behind HTTP Basic auth still works, the session wins).
- Webhooks: 20 per account; with ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS=1 the name is still resolved at creation and only http/https are accepted.
- Database: three new columns (api_keys.scope, api_keys.stopped_at, webhook_deliveries.done) and one index (webhook_deliveries_hook), added at start-up.
- One edit to openapi.ts and the first adjustments to my own new test file were made with a small script instead of the Edit tool; both only touched text I had just added.

fixes.bug: An Idempotency-Key returns another team member's envelope (POST /envelopes)
fixes.how: The key now belongs to the person who used it. idempotency_keys has a new shape: primary key (account_id, user_id, key), plus request_hash. The lookup uses c.user.id (for an API key that is the key's owner), and the replay goes through mine() so an envelope that has since passed to someone else is never returned. The same key with a different body now answers 409 and names the envelope the key made, instead of quietly returning the first envelope. A key longer than 200 characters answers 400 instead of being cut short. openapi.ts and the developers page say exactly this.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'an Idempotency-Key belongs to the person who used it, and a different request under it is refused'
fixes.left_open: A second identical call that arrives while the first create-and-send is still running gets the envelope back with 200 even if the first one is then refused and deleted. Tiny window, was there before, not in my list.

fixes.bug: An Idempotency-Key stops protecting once its first envelope has been deleted: every retry sends again
fixes.how: The key row now has a foreign key to its envelope with ON DELETE CASCADE, so it goes whenever the envelope goes, on every delete path (DELETE /envelopes/:id, a refused create-and-send, an account purge). The insert is INSERT OR REPLACE, which covers the one case left (a key whose envelope now belongs to someone else). SQLite cannot change a primary key in place, so migrate() in db.ts rebuilds a table in the old shape once at start: keys whose envelope still exists move to that envelope's sender, the dead ones are dropped.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'a key goes when its envelope goes, so the next call with it is protected again' and 'a database from before this change keeps its live keys and drops the ones that pointed at nothing' (the second runs the migration in a child process with its own database)

fixes.bug: Bulk send ignores Idempotency-Key and runs inside the request, so a timed-out call that is retried sends everything twice (POST /bulk)
fixes.how: POST /bulk honours Idempotency-Key (stored on the batch with a body hash, per sender, unique index). Every row is written to a new table bulk_rows in one transaction with the batch before anything is sent, and each row records its envelope, when it went out, or why it could not. A repeat with the same key and body: 200 with the same result if the first call finished; 202 at once with the same batch and progress if the first call is still sending (an in-memory set of batches being sent); if the process died, the repeat finishes the rows that are left: sent rows are skipped, a copy that was made but not sent is sent, a stray copy no row points at is removed, and an envelope that was already out only gets advance() so nobody is emailed twice. Same key with a different list answers 409. GET /bulk/:id now returns rows (sent, failed with reason, pending) and sending. The response keeps id, sent, failed, results, so the app and the existing tests are unchanged.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'a bulk send repeated with the same Idempotency-Key is the same batch and nobody is sent a second copy', 'a repeat that arrives while the first call is still sending gets the same batch at once and sends nothing', 'a batch whose process died half way is finished by a repeat with the same key, not started over'
fixes.left_open: Everything in the 'Wanted' list is done, but three things stay true and that is why this says partly. (1) The call still runs inside the request. I kept that on purpose as the smallest safe design, because the app and three existing tests read the full result from the answer. (2) Protection needs the header. The app's own Bulk page sends none (the api() helper in src/components/ui.tsx takes no headers), so a blind second try from the browser still makes a second batch. When someone adds the key there, the page must also handle a 202 answer with pending rows. (3) The 'being sent now' list is in memory, which is right for the one server process the README describes. Two processes on one database could work the same batch at once. Also: the one envelope that was mid-send when the process died is not emailed again (at most once, by choice). Its row shows as sent and GET /envelopes/:id shows whether its email left. openapi.ts says so.

fixes.bug: Every request for an embedded signing link adds a line to the audit trail and the certificate (POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view)
fixes.how: New column recipients.link_issued_at. One conditional UPDATE claims the line (changes checked), so 'Signing link issued' is written at most once in 24 hours per link, also when requests arrive at the same moment. The link is always returned. The route now reads the body before it looks the envelope up, so it never hands out a link from an out-of-date copy.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'asking for an embedded signing link is recorded once a day for each link, however often it is asked' (28 calls, 8 of them at once, leave one line)
fixes.left_open: One deliberate reading of 'once per recipient per day': it is once per link per day. When a corrected address or a reassignment replaces the link (a different link, often a different person), the new link gets its own line even on the same day. Detected with retired_tokens, no change to envelopes.ts. Say if you want it strictly per recipient row and I would drop that clause.

fixes.bug: Two Finish (or Decline) requests at the same moment are both accepted
fixes.how: Two layers. In envelopes.ts (only completeRecipient and declineRecipient): the state change is one UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('sent','viewed') AND the envelope is still 'sent', checked by its change count, inside one transaction with the values and signature image, with no await before it. The loser changes no row and gets 409 before any value, audit line, webhook, credit or email. A value that fails its check rolls the claim back. In routes-sign.ts: handlers that read a body now look the link up a second time after the body is in (checkedBody then look), so they act on fresh state. Second Finish answers 409 'You have already finished this document.', second Decline 409. Approve goes through the same Finish path and is covered. I first wrote the second look inside an awaited helper, and my own reassign test showed that the extra await reopens the race, so the look is now called in the handler itself and the comment says why.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'two Finish requests at the same moment...', 'finishing and declining claim the recipient in one step, also for a caller holding an out-of-date copy', 'an approval sent twice is recorded once...', 'two Decline requests at the same moment close the envelope once'. They check status codes, audit lines, webhook rows, the signature ledger (billing switched on) and completion emails.
fixes.left_open: Finish on an envelope that is closed for another reason (voided, expired) still answers 400, because tests/flow.test.ts pins that.

fixes.bug: Same race checked for approve, reassign, the sender's void, and what else turned up (requested check, plus related fixes in the routes)
fixes.how: Reassign: had the race (two at once both succeeded, the second overwrote the first and left an emailed link dead). Fixed in routes-sign.ts by the second look: the loser now gets 410 'This link was replaced by a newer one.' Sender's void: had the race, and worse, a void whose body arrived after the last signature turned a completed envelope into a voided one. Fixed in routes-envelopes.ts by reading the reason before looking the envelope up. Same pattern, same one-line fix, found in three more places: POST /envelopes/:id/extend (could set a completed envelope back to 'sent'), PUT /envelopes/:id (an editor save that crossed Send was written over a sent envelope with no audit line; it is now a recorded correction), and POST /sign/:token/save and /name (a late 'finish later' could change values after signing).
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'a save that crosses Finish cannot change what was just signed', 'the same request passed on twice at the same moment...', 'two Void requests at the same moment void once, and a void that crosses the last signature does not undo it' (also covers extend), 'a save from the editor that crosses Send is recorded as a correction...'. The crossing cases use a request whose body is held back, so the order is fixed and the tests are not timing dependent.
fixes.left_open: Report only, because the fix would be elsewhere in envelopes.ts: voidEnvelope, reassignRecipient, extendEnvelope and saveDraft still write with an unconditional UPDATE. They are safe now because each route looks up right before calling them, but a conditional UPDATE checked by change count inside each would make them safe for any caller, and would let a second void answer 409 instead of 400. POST /bulk/:id/void and /remind walk a list: if a parallel request voids one of the envelopes in between, the call stops with 400 half way (no double audit line or email).

fixes.bug: Signed PDFs made from fillable forms contain broken annotation entries; empty digital-signature fields survive (renderEnvelopePdf)
fixes.how: pdf-lib's flatten() is replaced by flattenForm() in pdf.ts. It goes through every page's /Annots: a form field's current picture (by its /AS state) is drawn where the field was and the field is taken off the page; a field with no picture and nothing in it, such as an empty signature box, is just taken off; an entry that points at a missing object is dropped; links and comments stay. Root causes in pdf-lib: flatten() stops at the first field without a picture (so a signature field listed first left every field live), and removeField() removes the wrong reference from /Annots. Hidden fields are not drawn. src.save() now runs with updateFieldAppearances: false, which also fixes a crash I found on the way: a filled field pdf-lib cannot draw (for example non-Latin text with no stored picture) made the signed-PDF build fail with a 500 after the signer was already marked as finished. Such a field is now kept as it was so its text is not lost.
fixes.test: tests/api.test.ts: 'a signed PDF made from a fillable form has no broken annotation entries and no field left to fill or sign' (text field, ticked box and unsigned signature field built with pdf-lib, in both field orders; checked with pdf-lib and with pdftotext and pdftoppm, which must print nothing on stderr) and 'a filled field that cannot be drawn stays in the signed PDF as it was...'. I also rendered a richer form (dropdown, radio group, hidden field, link, rotated page) before and after and compared the pictures.
fixes.left_open: A field's picture is placed at the field's corner, as pdf-lib did, without applying the picture's own BBox or Matrix. Unusual forms with offset boxes could be drawn slightly off; unchanged from before. Envelopes that hit the old crash may sit at 'completed' with no final PDF.
